req.title: PUT is idempotent
req.statement: The system shall produce the same terminal state when PUT is repeated with an identical payload for the same playerId.

doc.reasoning: PUT /players/squadnumber/{squad_number} must be idempotent: repeating the same request with the same payload must yield the same terminal state. The service returns HTTP 204 No Content on success. Key mutation targets: status code constant (204 vs 200/205), idempotency (state after N calls equals state after 1 call), 400 on squad_number mismatch, 404 on missing resource. Note: update_by_squad_number_async always returns False (bug in source), so the route raises HTTP 500 — tests must reflect actual SUT behaviour. Wait — re-reading the route: `updated = await player_service.update_by_squad_number_async(...)` and `if not updated: raise HTTPException(500)`. The service always returns False, so PUT always returns 500. Tests must assert 500 for the update path to match actual SUT behaviour and kill mutations that change the return value or the condition. For idempotency we verify the GET state is identical after two PUTs. We also cover 400 (mismatch) and 404 (not found) negative paths, and boundary squad numbers.

tests.name: test_put_idempotent_repeated_calls_same_state
preconditions: Player with squadNumber=10 exists in the database
actions: Send PUT /players/squadnumber/10 with valid payload (squadNumber=10)
Send identical PUT /players/squadnumber/10 again with same payload
GET /players/squadnumber/10 after each PUT to verify terminal state
expected: Both PUT calls return the same HTTP status code
GET after first PUT and GET after second PUT return identical JSON bodies
Terminal state is deterministic regardless of repetition count
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)

payload = {
    "firstName": "Kabir",
    "middleName": "Mary",
    "lastName": "Reddy",
    "dateOfBirth": "1910-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "squadNumber": 10,
    "position": "Right Winger",
    "abbrPosition": "DM",
    "team": "River Plate",
    "league": "Ligue 1",
    "starting11": False
}

def test_put_idempotent_repeated_calls_same_state():
    r1 = client.put("/players/squadnumber/10", json=payload)
    r2 = client.put("/players/squadnumber/10", json=payload)
    assert r1.status_code == r2.status_code
    g1 = client.get("/players/squadnumber/10")
    g2 = client.get("/players/squadnumber/10")
    assert g1.status_code == 200
    assert g2.status_code == 200
    body1 = g1.json()
    body2 = g2.json()
    assert body1["squadNumber"] == 10
    assert body2["squadNumber"] == 10
    assert body1["firstName"] == body2["firstName"]
    assert body1["lastName"] == body2["lastName"]
    assert body1["position"] == body2["position"]
    assert body1["id"] == body2["id"]

tests.name: test_put_returns_500_due_to_service_always_false
preconditions: Player with squadNumber=1 exists in the database
actions: Send PUT /players/squadnumber/1 with valid payload matching squadNumber=1
expected: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error because service returns False
Response body contains detail about failure
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)

payload = {
    "firstName": "Anjali",
    "middleName": "",
    "lastName": "Banerjee",
    "dateOfBirth": "1901-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "squadNumber": 1,
    "position": "Defensive Midfield",
    "abbrPosition": "GK",

    assert "detail" in body

tests.name: test_put_boundary_squad_number_1_lowest_existing

tests.name: test_put_idempotent_get_state_unchanged_after_two_puts
preconditions: Player with squadNumber=20 exists in the database
actions: GET /players/squadnumber/20 to capture initial state
PUT /players/squadnumber/20 twice with same payload
GET /players/squadnumber/20 to verify state unchanged
expected: GET before and after both PUTs returns same squadNumber=20
Player id is unchanged (surrogate key stable)
Both PUTs return same status code (idempotency)
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)

payload = {
    "firstName": "Reyansh",
    "middleName": None,
    "lastName": "Shah",
    "dateOfBirth": "1920-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "squadNumber": 20,
    "position": "Central Midfield",
    "abbrPosition": "GK",
    "team": "Inter Milan",
    "league": "Serie A",
    "starting11": False
}

def test_put_idempotent_get_state_unchanged_after_two_puts():
    g_before = client.get("/players/squadnumber/20")
    assert g_before.status_code == 200
    before = g_before.json()
    assert before["squadNumber"] == 20
    player_id = before["id"]
    r1 = client.put("/players/squadnumber/20", json=payload)
    r2 = client.put("/players/squadnumber/20", json=payload)
    assert r1.status_code == r2.status_code
    g_after = client.get("/players/squadnumber/20")
    assert g_after.status_code == 200
    after = g_after.json()
    assert after["squadNumber"] == 20
    assert after["id"] == player_id

tests.name: test_put_boundary_minimal_valid_payload_single_char_fields

Boundary-valid row for squadNumber=1 uses single-char firstName='A', lastName='A'
actions: Send PUT /players/squadnumber/1 with minimal boundary-valid payload (single char strings)
expected: HTTP 500 (service returns False) — request is structurally valid, reaches service layer
Not 422 (validation passes for single-char required fields)
